did_you_know.text: Did you know? Proverbs 12 opens by stating that those who love discipline love knowledge, while those who hate correction are described as foolish. The verse presents accepting criticism as part of wisdom.
Did you know? A virtuous wife is described as “a crown to her husband”—like a crown that brings honor—while a disgraceful wife is compared to decay in his bones, a picture of deep and lasting harm.

Did you know? The verse contrasts the words of the wicked, described as a deadly ambush, with the speech of the upright, which can save. Here, speech is presented as a force that can either harm or protect.
Did you know? Proverbs 12 explicitly mentions how people treat their animals: a righteous person knows and cares for the needs of his animal, while the compassion of the wicked is described as cruel.
Did you know? The verse favors meaningful work and a stable livelihood: those who work their land will have plenty of bread, unlike those who chase after empty pursuits.
Did you know? According to the verse, a fool considers his own way right, while a wise person listens to advice. Wisdom is linked here with a willingness to listen to others.

Did you know? Proverbs 12 compares hurtful speech to the thrusts of a sword, while describing the tongue of the wise as healing. This is a sharp contrast between verbal harm and encouragement that brings restoration.
Did you know? The verse states that truthful lips endure forever, while a lying tongue lasts only for a moment. Truth is presented as lasting, and lies as temporary.
Did you know? Proverbs 12 acknowledges that anxiety weighs heavily on a person’s heart and offers a good word as a source of joy. An encouraging word is presented as a means of bringing relief.

Did you know? The chapter concludes by stating that the way of righteousness leads to life, and that there is no death along its path. In this way, it sums up the ongoing contrast between the way of the righteous and the way of the wicked.
